arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: General Olson argued the case involves separation of powers. He stated the Constitution commits advisory authority to the President's discretion.

Mr. Morrison argued the threshold question is whether the Court of Appeals correctly ruled it lacked jurisdiction. He claimed the sides that brought the case painted a picture of being backed into a corner.
Mr. Orfanedes argued allegations and a memorandum raise significant questions. He suggested outside individuals may have participated in Vice President working groups.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This dispute defines the scope of judicial power over executive branch internal processes. It determines whether courts can scrutinize how the Vice President organizes staff and policy advice. The outcome clarifies the limits of separation of powers in administrative law.
